lesson_title: Feeding the Crocodile: The Road to 1 September 1939
hook_text: Every time they gave Hitler what he wanted, he came back for more. Here is how appeasement led straight to war.
clip_script: Hitler had a plan: tear up the Treaty of Versailles, unite all Germans, and grab living space in the east. Then he tested the fence. 1935: a new army and air force, both banned. Nothing. 1936: troops into the Rhineland. He admitted later that if France had fought, he would have retreated. France did nothing. 1938: Austria swallowed. Then the Sudetenland of Czechoslovakia. At Munich, Britain and France agreed to hand it over. Czechoslovakia was not even in the room. Chamberlain flew home: peace for our time. Churchill warned that an appeaser feeds a crocodile, hoping it will eat him last. Six months later, Hitler took the rest of Czechoslovakia. August 1939: Hitler and Stalin sign a secret deal to split Poland. 1 September: tanks and dive-bombers roll into Poland. 3 September: Britain and France declare war. And in Cape Town, Parliament votes 80 to 67 to join them. World War II has begun.
visual_style: A map of Europe with Germany growing step by step: Rhineland, Austria, Sudetenland, Czechia; a crocodile shadow grows with each bite; a paper waved at an airport; two dictators' signatures; tanks crossing into Poland; a parliament vote counter at 80 to 67.
pacing: Quick steps with a beat after each, a pause on Munich, a rapid final sequence to war.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for the reasons behind appeasement, the Nazi-Soviet Pact and the Axis and Allies.
